jsonld.description: Monthly website maintenance: updates, backups, security, uptime monitoring, speed upkeep, content edits and reporting.

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the routine work that keeps a site secure, fast and up to date: software updates, backups, security checks, uptime monitoring, speed upkeep and small content changes.

mainEntity.name: What is included in your website maintenance plans?

acceptedAnswer.text: Updates, backups, security scans, uptime monitoring, speed checks, broken link fixes, small content edits and a monthly report. The comparison table on this page shows what each level covers.

mainEntity.name: Do you maintain sites you did not build?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We audit the site first, fix urgent issues and then bring it onto the routine. We may suggest changes if the build makes upkeep risky.

mainEntity.name: Do you only maintain WordPress sites?

acceptedAnswer.text: WordPress is the most common, and we also look after custom builds and other CMS sites. Tell us the platform and we will confirm.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my site is hacked?

acceptedAnswer.text: We restore from a clean backup, remove the malware, close the way in and report what happened. Cleanup is scoped on a call if the site is already infected.
You send a request by email or a shared board, and we make the change within the agreed hours. Larger changes are quoted before we start.
It depends on the platform, the size of the site and how much editing you need. Talk to us and we will recommend a level and write the scope down.

hub.sub: Updates, backups, security, uptime, speed, content edits and a monthly report, on a retainer that fits how often your site changes.

answer.label: In short
answer.lead: Website maintenance is the routine care that keeps a site secure, fast and current: software updates, backups, security checks, uptime monitoring, speed upkeep and small content edits. A retainer makes these a monthly habit, so problems are fixed before visitors or search engines notice.
answer.who: Monday Marketing Company (MMC) maintains WordPress and other sites for B2B, education and D2C brands, whether or not we built them.

points.title: Security and uptime

points.title: Monthly report

answer.chip: A site that is looked after every month

paras: Most site problems are not dramatic. An outdated plugin, a failed form, a slow page or an expired certificate quietly costs enquiries for weeks. A retainer puts someone on the checklist every month.
We work on WordPress most often, and also on custom and other CMS sites. If we built your site with our WordPress development team, we already know how it is put together.

blocks.h: What each level of care covers
paras: We describe three levels of care. The right one depends on how often your site changes and how much it earns. Talk to us and we will suggest a level and write down exactly what is included.

callout.text: Tell us how often you update the site and what it earns. We will recommend one on a call. Agencies can also use our white-label website maintenance.

grid.lede: Six jobs done every month, so you do not have to remember them.

items.d: WordPress core, plugins and themes updated on a schedule, tested first on a staging copy where possible.
Regular off-site backups with a tested restore, so a bad update is reversible.
Malware scans, login protection, firewall rules and fixes for known vulnerabilities.
Monitoring with alerts, plus image, script and caching upkeep to keep pages quick.
Small text, image, banner and page changes done for you within the agreed hours.
What was updated, what was fixed, what to watch and what we suggest next.

leaks.lede: A site that is cared for keeps earning its place. Each stage below is where care slips, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Updating a site nobody has audited.
stages.why: Old plugins, weak hosting and missing backups stay hidden until something breaks.
stages.does: We check versions, plugins, hosting, backups, security and speed, and list what needs fixing first.

stages.breaks: Updates run straight on the live site.
stages.why: One bad update can break a layout or a form.
stages.does: We set up backups and monitoring, and a safe copy to test updates before they go live.

stages.why: Scans, checks and small edits slip when nobody owns them.
stages.does: Updates, scans, checks and small edits happen on a schedule you can see.

stages.breaks: No record of what was done.
stages.why: Without a summary you cannot tell what was fixed or what comes next.
stages.does: Each month you get a summary, and we suggest changes worth making next.

process.note: Timing depends on scope. We agree it with you before work starts.
